messages.author: 5f61b2567c25daf9
messages.subject: export tree
parts:
Hello,

I am new to poppr. I was able to load, convert and run my analysis correctly. However, I was wondering if there is any option to export a tree in a generic forma (e.g. newick) to load in specific tree rendering programs.

Any help is appreciated.
Best,
Thiago

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: export tree
parts:
Hi Thiago,

You can export a tree using the function "write.nexus" from the package "ape".

Special tip: If you want to add tip colors to your tree for use in FigTree, you can use the function add.tip.colors from this gist.

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: export tree
parts:
Dear Zhian,

Thanks for the prompt response. Yes, I always go for Figtree.
I tried write.nexus, but got the following error:

arog <- aboot(obj, dist = rogers.dist, sample = 1000)
write.nexus(arog,"test.nexus")

OUTPUT:
BEGIN TAXA;
        DIMENSIONS NTAX = 90;
        TAXLABELS

90 genotypes...

        ;
END;
BEGIN TREES;
        TRANSLATE

Error in y$tip.label : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

Do you know how to solve this issue ?
Best,
Thiago

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Re: export tree
parts:
Hi Thiago,

You can compare populations by converting your data to a genpop object:

obj.pop <- genind2genpop(obj)

proj <- aboot(obj.pop, sample = 1000, dist = rogers.dist) # This should go really fast.

Cheers,
Zhian
